title: Paytm wallet could return: RBI grants Paytm Payments Services in-principle PPI authorisation
summary: RBI grants Paytm Payments Services in-principle PPI authorisation signaling wallet return
detailed: Paytm's payments subsidiary, Paytm Payments Services Limited (PPSL), has received in-principle authorisation from the RBI to issue prepaid payment instruments (PPIs), including digital wallets.
The approval puts the fintech company on course to restart a wallet business that was frozen when the RBI acted against Paytm Payments Bank in 2024.

One 97 Communications, the listed parent of Paytm, said the RBI's Department of Payment and Settlement Systems granted the authorisation in a letter dated 13 November, under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
The RBI granted PPSL in-principle authorisation to operate as an online payment aggregator on 12 August 2025, lifting restrictions on onboarding new online merchants.
sentences: Paytm's payments subsidiary, Paytm Payments Services Limited (PPSL), has received in-principle authorisation from the RBI to issue prepaid payment instruments (PPIs), including digital wallets.
The approval puts the fintech company on course to restart a wallet business that was frozen when the RBI acted against Paytm Payments Bank in 2024.

One 97 Communications, the listed parent of Paytm, said the RBI's Department of Payment and Settlement Systems granted the authorisation in a letter dated 13 November, under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.

The authorisation allows PPSL to set up and operate a payment system for issuing and operating PPIs in India, subject to the RBI's Master Directions on Prepaid Payment Instruments dated 27 August 2021.
The wallet cannot be launched straight away.
The company said PPSL can offer prepaid instruments such as a wallet to customers only after it receives the final authorisation, or Certificate of Authorisation, from the RBI.
According to reports, PPSL must complete a system audit, including a cybersecurity audit, and submit the report to the RBI within six months.
If it misses that deadline, the in-principle authorisation lapses.
Paytm first flagged the application in its Q1 FY27 earnings release in July.
Answering the question “ When can we expect wallet to come back? ”, the company wrote that PPSL had applied for a wallet licence.
“ We believe that consumers benefit from a range of payment options and wallet will add to completeness of our consumer offerings, ” the company stated.
The Paytm wallet was earlier run through Paytm Payments Bank.
The RBI had barred the bank from onboarding new customers in March 2022.
On 31 January 2024, the regulator ordered the bank to stop accepting deposits, credit transactions and top-ups in customer accounts, wallets, FASTags and NCMC cards after 29 February 2024.
It said a comprehensive system audit and a later compliance validation report had found “ persistent non-compliances and continued material supervisory concerns in the bank ”.
Customers could still withdraw or use their existing balances, but could no longer add money to their wallets.
The RBI then cancelled the bank's licence with effect from the close of business on 24 April 2026, under Section 22(4) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

The regulator said the general character of the bank's management was “ prejudicial to the interest of depositors as also the public interest ”, and that the bank had failed to comply with the conditions of its payments bank licence.
It said the bank had enough liquidity to repay depositors when it is wound up.
The new approval has gone to PPSL, a wholly owned subsidiary of One 97 Communications, and not to the payments bank.
The approval comes weeks after Paytm reported its highest quarterly EBITDA so far.
In the September quarter, consolidated revenue from operations rose 28% year-on-year to Rs 2,648 crore and EBITDA rose 90% to Rs 270 crore.
Net profit was Rs 225 crore, against Rs 21 crore a year earlier.
Paytm had an average of 8.5 crore monthly transacting users in the quarter, up 1 crore from a year earlier, and said it gained consumer payments market share for a sixth straight quarter.
Its Soundbox devices are deployed at 1.64 crore storefronts, and it reported a cash balance of Rs 13,617 crore.
The company has said the MDR framework notified by NPCI for select UPI merchant payments would be an upside rather than the foundation of its business.
Based on the proposed 0.4% cap on select payments above Rs 2,000, it expects an indicative uplift of about 2.5 basis points in its payment processing margin.
The wallet approval follows a long road to PPSL's payment aggregator licence.
PPSL first applied for that licence in November 2020.
The RBI rejected the application in November 2022, asked the company to reapply in compliance with Press Note 3 under foreign direct investment rules, and barred PPSL from onboarding new merchants.
The RBI granted PPSL in-principle authorisation to operate as an online payment aggregator on 12 August 2025, lifting restrictions on onboarding new online merchants.
It issued the final Certificate of Authorisation on 26 November 2025, about three months later.
Paytm has also transferred its offline merchant payments business, which includes QR-code payments, Soundbox devices and card machines, to PPSL, effective 30 November 2025.
